start.text: That's Mara's gull on your token. Right, then. Right.
Stay on the boardwalk. Keep that ember high. And if you start forgetting why you went — turn round, that's what she told us.

shut.text: Lofts are shut. Harbormaster's orders. Folk go in for a net and come out asking whose net it is.
You want past, you want Mara's say-so. Brass, with a gull on it.

choice.text: Mara says you paced the bank with an oar.

choice.note: Day 122: the lit ending, Brenner out on the cod grounds.

lofts.text: The net-lofts, then the headland, then the Gull's Beacon. Used to be you could see it from the harbor. Now you can't see your own boots past the third loft.

hesk.text: Old Hesk. Wouldn't come out when the rest of us ran. She's still up there mending, humming. She won't know you.
She taught me every knot I've got. Doesn't know my name now.

start_lit.text: I can see the beacon from the gate. First time since the Snuffing. I keep looking, in case it goes out.
Rang the gate bell when Dunstan came round the breakwater. Rowing backward, lantern in the stern, laughing at the gulls. I rang it like he was a fire. Nobody's said a word against it.
Big man rowed in on the evening tide facing backward, lantern in the stern. I rang the gate bell like he was a fire. Don't ask me why. It seemed owed.
Hesk's stopped humming. The lofts are quiet as a church. I don't know if that's better.

ferry_fare.text: Saw it go up. The whole gate crew stood and stared at it like it was a sunrise.
You'll want to know how it goes, with us. Tidewrights don't sell a crossing, not the old way. You pay the lanes a deed, and the ferry's crew weighs it.
Most folk bring a mended hull, or a drowned man's name carried home. You brought the Gull back. That'll weigh.
Mind, some of the crew'll ask what it cost. Tidewrights tie nets too. Don't expect them all to thank you for the knot.

ferry_in.text: Half the gate crew's down the dock pretending to check lines. That's the Slow Mercy. Oda Farrow's. She taught me my first hitch.
If she weighs you light, don't argue. Nobody's ever won an argument with Oda. Not even the sea.

bank_paced.text: Out to the outer post in Brenner's boat, and on from there with the oar laid flat across the bow, so I'd know the moment the grey touched it.
Touched at four lengths. Thin as breath on a window. I said it out loud: four. Brenner wanted to keep going. I sat on his oars.
Rowed back singing. Not any song. I just wanted noise in the boat, and there wasn't any tune to hand.
It lies out there like a net with nobody hauling. I keep saying things like that. Mara lets me.
Brenner kept looking back over his shoulder all the way in. Like there ought to be another boat behind us.

brenner_out.text: Out on the cod grounds. Every tide that'll have him. You can see him from the gate if you know where to look: past the post, a speck with a cap on.
Tells everyone you told him to go, back before it was safe. He's prouder of that than of the cod.
Says you told him to wait, and he did, and it was worth it. He says it like it was his own idea.
